## Design

### 2026-11-01: My 8-Hour PCB Design Marathon

**8h**

My 8-Hour PCB Design Marathon

Today was an absolute grind, spending a solid 8 hours working on the PaperRead e-reader board. What I thought would be a quick routing session turned into a full-on marathon of fixing errors, routing traces, and getting the double-sided PCB looking clean.

* Setup and Layout: Locked down the core layout with the Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C3 (U1), wired up the 3 tactile push buttons (SW1–SW3) for controls, connected the slide power switch (SW6) to the battery header (J3), and added the e-paper display header (J1). I also switched over to a compact 3.3V MicroSD card module (J2) tied right to the 3.3V rail so reading text files will be super smooth.
* Footprint and Routing Hurdles: Hit a bunch of annoying footprint pin mismatch errors right at the start, which meant hunting down the right RF_Module:MCU_Seeed_ESP32C3 footprint in KiCad. Routing all the traces on such a compact board took a lot of patience to make sure power and data lines didn't cross weirdly.
* Aesthetics and Copper Pours: I wanted to give the board some personality, so I added some custom vector art (a starfish, a giraffe, a moon, and text). The big catch was making sure none of the artwork touched the copper pads, otherwise soldering would fail. Finally, I added four corner mounting holes and flooded both layers with a solid GND copper pour to keep electrical noise away.
* Milestone Reached: After running a final Design Rules Check (DRC) to clear out any last-minute issues, I successfully exported the whole thing as a 3D STEP file.

Eight hours well spent—the board looks awesome, the hardware connections are solid, and it's officially ready for the

Journal Entry: Writing the PaperRead Firmware

Spent a good chunk of time today getting the firmware for the PaperRead e-reader up and running in the Arduino IDE. Writing code for e-paper displays is always a little different compared to regular LCDs or OLEDs, but everything is starting to come together nicely.

* Library Setup & Display: Got the GxEPD2 library dialed in for the e-paper panel, making sure the SPI pins, data/command (DC), reset, and busy pins match the schematic layout. The slow refresh rate of e-paper makes it feel like a real book page-turn!
* MicroSD Integration: Tied the SD card module into the SPI bus using the proper chip select pin. Tested reading text files off the card so the reader can pull up stories or text documents directly from the root directory.
* Button Mapping: Configured the 3 tactile push buttons (previous page, next page, and select/refresh) with proper debouncing logic so inputs are clean and responsive without accidental double-clicks.
